text.text: The Dragon 32 was an 8-bit home computer released in 1982 by Dragon Data in Wales, United Kingdom. Based around the Motorola 6809E processor, it shared many similarities with the Tandy TRS-80 Color Computer while adding a full-size keyboard and a strong BASIC programming environment. The system was used for education, programming, and gaming, with software available through cassette tapes, cartridges, and disk expansions. Although commercially short-lived, the Dragon 32 developed a dedicated following among retro computing enthusiasts.
